clue.text: Game for basketball experts?

parts.note: not the hoops game: a Basque court game whose players sling the ball from a long curved wicker basket strapped to the wrist

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which sport suits people who are good at basketball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basketball' suggests the American hoops game, but read it as 'basket-ball': in this Basque game the ball is caught and hurled with a wicker basket called a cesta.
explanation.definitionFit: This jai alai-style sport is played with a curved wickerwork scoop, so its players are literally experts with basket and ball.

clue.text: Hand on or ignore

definitions.meaning: to give something to the next person

explanation.definitionFit: To give something along is one sense; to skip over or disregard someone, as for promotion, is the other.

clue.text: His plight may serve as a warning to sailors

definitions.text: His plight may serve as a warning to sailors

parts.words: His plight may serve as a warning to sailors
parts.note: read not as a cautionary tale of a shipwrecked man but as a moored vessel whose light warns shipping

explanation.surface: A sailor's sad fate is a lesson to others at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His plight' looks like a man's misfortune, but it hides 'his p-light': a ship (sailors' 'she') with a light, anchored as a beacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored vessel carrying a beacon marks hazards and warns passing ships.

clue.text: Cutting pastry

definitions.meaning: a cutting remark is sharp or sour
a pastry case with a sweet filling

explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, acid remark is cutting; a fruit-filled pastry dish is the second sense.

clue.text: All too human story in which evil makes a comeback

indicators.note: the story contains the next piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

indicators.note: coming back means the word for evil is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ill as a noun means evil or harm

explanation.surface: A tale in which wickedness returns, and the characters prove all too human.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evil' reads as an adjective in the surface, but here it is the noun ill; 'makes a comeback' turns it round and 'in which' places it in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is human, so someone prone to mistakes is merely mortal and imperfect.

clue.text: And to us, possibly, it will seem surprising

definitions.note: the clue's 'it will seem surprising' describes what the verb does: to shock with wonder

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters might form something else in another order

explanation.surface: Someone saying that, to the rest of us, it will come as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AND TO US; 'it will seem surprising' wraps the definition, since what astounds seems amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze or stun someone is to be greatly surprising to them.

clue.text: No salt!

parts.note: not a cook's warning but a 'salt' is an old sailor, so this is someone who is no seaman

explanation.surface: A cook's or doctor's order to leave out the salt.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'old salt' is a seasoned sailor, so 'no salt' is someone happier ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A person unused to the sea, clumsy aboard ship, is the opposite of a seasoned sailor.

clue.text: Animated youngster in book given limited scope

indicators.note: limited means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: ambit means scope or extent

explanation.surface: A young person full of life appears in a book with little room to manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'given' are links; 'limited' clips AMBIT to AMBI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney cartoon fawn is a young deer brought to life on screen.

clue.text: Describing one with the most experience of life

definitions.text: Describing one with the most experience of life

parts.words: Describing one with the most experience of life
parts.note: not wisdom but simple age: the sibling who has lived longest

explanation.surface: Describing the wisest, most worldly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Experience of life' suggests worldly wisdom, but it means only years lived.
explanation.definitionFit: The firstborn child, oldest of a family, has been alive the longest.

clue.text: Still good advice to the over-excited

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to make calm or quiet
the words '...', told to someone agitated

explanation.definitionFit: To bring a ship to a halt for lack of wind is to make it still; split, it tells an agitated person to settle down.

clue.text: But grease can also be extracted from this plant

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase can be pulled out and re-formed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that this crop yields grease as well as its usual product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can also be extracted from' rearranges the nine letters of BUT GREASE; the surface plays on sugar, not grease, being what is really extracted from the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A root crop grown in temperate countries as a source of table sugar is a plant.

clue.text: He has no settled occupation

parts.note: read not as a man without a steady job but as one who occupies no fixed home, wandering from place to place

explanation.surface: Describing a man who drifts between jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' looks like a career, but here it means occupying a place: a wanderer settles nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer without a fixed dwelling, moving with herds or seasons, has no settled place to live.

clue.text: Food of love at first sight

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the round letter O

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is all that is taken

explanation.surface: A romantic phrase, love at first sight, made into a menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; O (love, a zero score in tennis) plus AT plus the first letter of 'sight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain eaten as porridge, or fed to horses, is a staple foodstuff.

clue.text: They have suffered from offhand relationships

parts.note: an offhand manner is casual
ties are bonds or relationships

explanation.surface: People hurt by careless affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Victims of accidents or battles are those who have been killed or injured.

clue.text: Justifying fighting talk

parts.note: war is fighting
ranting is wild, loud talk

explanation.surface: Defending aggressive rhetoric.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving good grounds for something is to justify it.

clue.text: I hamper arrangement made for Joseph's son

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters means they are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone saying they are getting in the way of plans made for a man named Joseph's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made for' is a link joining the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the patriarch Joseph had two sons, Manasseh and the younger one who founded a tribe of Israel.

clue.text: Be back in time for the discussion

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: back means the little word is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to return punctually for the talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be back' sounds like a request to return; it is the wordplay, with 'back' turning the little word and 'in' placing it within the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument in which opposing views are aired is a discussion.

clue.text: Act concerning a volte-face

parts.note: a turn is an act on stage
about means concerning

explanation.surface: A theatrical performance on the subject of a sudden change of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of policy or opinion is a U-turn.

clue.text: Cricketer yearns to be a spinner

parts.note: to long is to yearn
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricketer who wants to become a spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link. 'Spinner' suggests a spin bowler, but gives the toy TOP. A LONG-STOP is a fielder placed far behind the wicketkeeper in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielding position directly behind the wicketkeeper near the boundary names the player who stands there.

clue.text: Spares may be few and far between

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could become another word if reordered

explanation.surface: Spare parts may be hard to come by.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly scattered things are scarce, with gaps between them.

clue.text: Straying sheep lead us to Biblical city

indicators.note: the first piece leads, coming in front of the last word
straying sheep wander about, so the letters move out of order

explanation.surface: Lost sheep guide us to a city in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is a verb in the surface (sheep guiding us) and still means precede in the wordplay: the scrambled flock comes first, before 'us'. Ephesus was a city in Asia Minor.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Ionian city in modern Turkey received one of Paul's epistles in the New Testament.

clue.text: One is going to say it

definitions.text: One is going to say it

parts.words: One is going to say it
parts.note: not a person about to speak but someone who is leaving, who says a farewell

explanation.surface: Someone is about to speak up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is going' reads as 'is about to', but it means 'is departing': a departing person says this.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery British goodbye is what a person leaving says.

clue.text: Slightly exaggerate account and blush

definitions.meaning: to ... a story is to embellish or slant it
to go red in the face

explanation.definitionFit: To embellish or distort a story slightly is to tint it; reddening with embarrassment is the second sense.

clue.text: Burning with fresh after a bad start

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Burning with fresh after a bad start' (6): A + B (bad start) + LAZE (fresh anagram of ZEAL) needs a word ZEAL not in the clue as held; no source found for the full text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Burning with fresh after a bad start

clue.text: An original idea to mind the baby

parts.note: the brain is the mind
a baby is a child

explanation.surface: An inventive notion to babysit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'mind' looks like a verb (look after) but gives the noun BRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's invention or creation, born of their own thinking, is an original idea.

clue.text: Young Victorian heroine caught in a lie

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the next words

parts.note: taken as written, the two words together
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A young heroine of the nineteenth century is found out in a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside A LIE. The heroine is Lewis Carroll's Victorian girl who visits Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's girl who falls down a rabbit hole is a young heroine of the Victorian era.

clue.text: Suspend for a mild expletive

definitions.meaning: to suspend is to fix something so it dangles
as in '... it all!', a gentle oath

explanation.definitionFit: To dangle from a hook is to be suspended; 'hang it!' is an old-fashioned softened curse.

clue.text: Chapter-head

parts.note: not the heading of a book's chapter but the head of a cathedral chapter, its governing body of clergy

explanation.surface: A heading at the start of a chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: A chapter is also the body of canons running a cathedral, and its head is this clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior clergyman presiding over a cathedral's governing chapter leads it.

clue.text: An out-of-the-way plea

parts.note: not an obscure request but a legal defence that one was elsewhere, away from the scene

explanation.surface: An odd or remote request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-the-way' suggests obscure, but literally means being somewhere else when a crime happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'elsewhere', it is the defence that the accused was away from the scene.

clue.text: The craft of dressing?

parts.note: not the skill of clothing oneself but a vessel, a boat-shaped jug, that carries a dressing such as gravy

explanation.surface: A question about the art of putting on clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like skill and 'dressing' like clothing; read 'craft' as a vessel and 'dressing' as a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat-shaped jug for serving gravy carries a dressing, so it is the dressing's vessel.

clue.text: Greene is about to liven things up

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The novelist Graham Greene is about to brighten things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about to' reads as 'is going to', but 'about' is the anagram signal on GREENE IS, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To give vigour or zest to something is to put life into it.

clue.text: A section of the foot soldiers should be

definitions.meaning: the arched upper part of the foot between toes and ankle
marching troops should keep pace together

explanation.definitionFit: The arch of the foot is one part of it; marching troops keep in step, moving in unison.
